blank_check.what: every written PNG is decoded and its luminance measured; a uniform image is the known Vulkan failure (leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp#1031: blank PNG, exit success)
blank_check.bound: blank when spread <= 2/255 AND stdev <= 1.0, or alpha is 0 everywhere sampled

resume.what: recipe = prompt + negative(if it can act) + size + cfg + steps + seed; a match is skipped, a mismatch is made again
resume.record: made.json 5 item(s); the previous manifest 0 recorded + 0 reconstructed; 5 item(s) on record in total

negatives.what: --negative-prompt is passed whenever an item has one; it only ACTS when cfg != 1.0, because sd-cli evaluates the unconditional branch only then

selection.what: only = the ids asked for by name; limit = how many pictures this run may GENERATE, which skipped items do not count against

images.binds_to: CANDIDATE FOR THE HOOK SHEET'S STREET PANEL - pass 4, aimed only at pass 3's two remaining faults: Mickey's as one bay of the terrace, and on the left.
images.prompt: the view filling the frame edge to edge, Use case: historical-scene. One photoreal pedestrian eye-height concept panel for LEDGER, the fictional British port town Meridian, a wet overcast working weekday in 1990. The camera stands 1.6 m high in the carriageway at the SOUTH END of Quay Street, LOOKING NORTH up the street. THE SUBJECT IS THE TERRACE ON THE LEFT: one continuous two-storey red and soot brick party-wall terrace running away from the camera up the left side of the street in repeated 6 m bays, every bay the same height and joined to the next, one unbroken slate roof with party-wall chimney stacks on it, one unbroken building line along the pavement, tall narrow white two-over-two sash windows upstairs under flat brick arches. THE NEAREST BAY OF THAT TERRACE, on the left, is MICKEY'S, a small minicab office, built into the row exactly like its neighbours with the same roof, the same upper windows and the same brick above it, and a shop hard against it on its far side: its old shopfront has been replaced by a flat aluminium window unit of thin dark metal sections set flat against the bare brickwork, a wide sheet of plate glass, a flat metal door with a long push bar, a cold white fluorescent tube behind the glass, a hand-lettered card taped inside the window, a bare counter with a two-way radio set and an open hardbacked fare book on it, a patterned glazed tile stallriser below the glass, raw new brick repair patches around the opening, and one plain painted fascia board over it reading MICKEY'S in plain painted capitals. ONE OR TWO ORDINARY UNMARKED PRIVATE SALOON CARS, plain and second hand, are parked at the kerb directly outside it. The other shop bays further up the terrace have painted fascia boards too far off and too rain-streaked for their lettering to be read. ON THE RIGHT, across the road, the street opens out: a lower terrace of plain brick houses set back behind the far pavement. 6 m wet asphalt carriageway with a crowned camber, a white centre line, double yellow lines along both kerbs, 2 m stone flag pavements with a kerb. Worn where water and hands put it and clean elsewhere: black soot streaks below one leaking gutter, a dark splashed foot to the walls along the busiest stretch of pavement, flaking paint on the older joinery, and a well-kept front among the worn ones. Two or three ordinary working people at different distances in 1990 British clothes, seen from behind or too far off for a face to read. At the far end of the street the ground rises inland into contour-following brick terraces stepping up the slope behind stone retaining walls, pale and soft in the haze. Photoreal throughout, photographic material plausibility, soft directionless overcast light under a flat white sky., invented fictional shop name only, no real company names, no real brand logos, no trade marks, no real person, no recognisable faces, no celebrity likeness, no alcohol and no gambling anywhere in frame, nothing poured or consumed, no games of chance, nobody under eighteen and no school in use, nothing sexual
